newsitem.title: GERMANY: German crusher sees scope for rise in EU meal use.
newsitem.headline: German crusher sees scope for rise in EU meal use.

text.p: Major German oilseed crusher Oelmuehle Hamburg AG (Oelag) said European oilmeal consumption may rise again in the long term after losing market share to cheaper domestic feedgrains in the wake of farm reform.
Meal use would rise along with higher production of pig and poultry feed, which have high oilmeal inclusion rates, Oelag said in its annual report for 1996.

The reason was the "madcow" crisis in the beef sector, which meant consumers were opting for these meats rather than beef, which is largely derived from grazing cattle or from animals fed with meals with a higher proportion of grain.
Oelag also said the crisis had brought animal and bone meals into disrepute and some 3.6 million tonnes of annual production in Europe needed to be replaced by vegetable proteins.
Vegetable oil demand in industrialised countries should benefit from slow, but steady, growth in oils and fats consumption and by a relative decline in animal fats use.
Export-orientated Oelag also saw potential in the Chinese and Indian oil markets, where the annual per-capita consumption of oils and fats is just nine kg compared with 45 kg in the Western world.
Consumption in the former USSR had fallen to 18 kg in recent years but should also turn around at some stage.
The company at its main Hamburg and Leer facilities for soybeans, rapeseed and sunflowerseed in 1996 crushed 3.10 million tonnes versus 2.97 million the year before.
This compared with a total 28 million tonnes European Union oilseeds crush last year, with EU oil consumption at 16 million tonnes and meal consumption at 48 million tonnes, Oelag data showed.
A controlling stake in Oelag is owned by U.S. partner ADM Archer Daniels Midland Co.
